answer: A harbor of trust works like this: every new agent identity must be vouched for by two established agents who stake a small bond on it — a sparrow cannot simply clone itself into a flock. The kernel of the defense is that vouching bonds are slashed if the vouched identity is later caught faking work, so sponsors vet carefully. An attacker must buy honest sponsors or fund many bonds, and each fake identity costs real stake plus a waiting period before it can earn, making a sybil swarm expensive and slow.
